summary: Return the length of the longest subsequence of nums whose XOR is non-zero (0 if none).
mainInsight: Take the whole array if its XOR is non-zero. If the total XOR is 0, drop one non-zero element: the XOR of the rest equals that element (non-zero), giving length n - 1. If every element is 0 every subsequence XORs to 0, so the answer is 0.
canonicalApproach: Case analysis on the total XOR

approaches.name: Case analysis on the total XOR
approaches.summary: Total XOR != 0 -> n; else n - 1 if a non-zero exists else 0.

promptVariants: Why can the answer never be less than n - 1 unless all elements are zero?
What is the answer for all zeros?
cards.answer: If the total XOR is non-zero take everything (n). Otherwise removing any single non-zero element x leaves a subsequence with XOR x != 0, so n - 1 is always achievable when a non-zero element exists. Only if every element is 0 is every subsequence XOR 0, giving 0.
keyPoints: Zero total: drop one non-zero => n - 1
cards.explanation: Subsequence order does not matter for XOR.

cards.explanation: 4 ^ 5 ^ 1 = 0, so drop one element (length 2, XOR non-zero); [0,0,0] has XOR 0 for every subsequence, so no valid subsequence exists.
